chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Al-Sheikh (peace be upon him) that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
passed away and left sixty slaves, so I emancipated a third of them, drawing lots between them, and extracted the third.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam determine which slaves to free when emancipating a portion of a deceased person's slaves?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of manumission (itq) by Imam al-Baqir (AS) following the death of his father, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), who bequeathed sixty slaves. By freeing one-third and using lots to select them, the Imam demonstrated a methodical approach to fulfilling the bequest, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the merit of liberating slaves as a form of charity and spiritual purification.
